title: o_e, oe, u_e and ew
overview:
New spellings: o_e, oe, u_e, ue, ew.
Long o and long u. And a second sound for ow.
Two letters. One sound.
Do not sound them out one by one.
functions: Say the sound for each new spelling
Read a word that has one in it
Write a word that has one in it
Know where in a word each one goes
Read the new words out loud
Choose between two spellings of one sound
learningPath: Words: the new spellings and the new words.
Write the words from their sounds.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 17. Long o and long u.
You know long o. You met it as oa.
Boat. Coat. That is the sound.
Here is another. O_e. The silent e again.
Not. Now add an e. Note.
The e reaches back and makes the o long.
Home. h. o_e. m. Three sounds.
And one more. Oe. Toe. Goes.
There are not many of those. Learn the few.
Now something you have already met.
In Unit 14 you learned ow. Cow. Now.
But listen to this word. Slow.
Slow. That is not the cow sound.
That is long o.
Ow has two sounds. Cow and slow.
Same as oo in Unit 13. Boot and foot.
Try one. If it is not a word, try the other.
Now long u. You have it as oo. Boot.
Three more ways to write it.
U_e. June. J. u_e. n. Three sounds.
Ue. Blue. b. l. ue. Three sounds.
Ew. New. n. ew. Two sounds.
Careful with ew. It is not ow.
New is not now. Look at the letters.
So long o has four spellings.
Oa, o_e, ow and oe.
And long u has four.
Oo, u_e, ue and ew.
That is Unit 17. Two sounds, eight spellings.

grammar.title: The new spellings: o_e, oe, u_e, ue, ew
grammar.explanation:
No new sounds. Long o and long u again.
You had long o as oa. You had long u as oo.
These are five more ways to write them.
grammar.rule:
o_e   as in home    h - o_e - m
oe    as in toe     t - oe
u_e   as in June    J - u_e - n
ue    as in blue    b - l - ue
ew    as in new     n - ew
grammar.workedExample:
You see o_e in a word.
1. Do not read two letters.
2. Read one sound.
3. Say that sound out loud.
4. Now find it in home.
5. Say the sound again there.
grammar.mistake:
Sounding out both letters gives no word at all.
home is not h - o - m - e.
It is h - o_e - m.
grammar.tip: Two letters. Look once. Say once.
grammar.practice:
Say the sound for each one.
1. o_e
2. oe
3. u_e
4. ue
5. ew
grammar.answers:
Check yourself out loud.
Did you say ONE sound each time?
Two sounds means you read the letters, not the spelling.

grammar.title: Reading a word that has o_e, oe, u_e, ue, ew in it
grammar.explanation:
Find the two letters first.
Read them as one sound.
Then read the rest of the word.
grammar.rule:
home     h - o_e - m
slow     s - l - ow
toe      t - oe
June     J - u_e - n
blue     b - l - ue
new      n - ew
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word slow.
1. Look for the two letters.
2. Cover them with your finger.
3. Read what is left.
4. Now put the one sound back in.
5. Join it all. slow.
grammar.mistake:
Reading left to right, letter by letter, breaks here.
Look for the pair BEFORE you start.
grammar.practice:
Join the sounds and write the word.
1. h - o_e - m
2. s - l - ow
3. t - oe
4. J - u_e - n
5. b - l - ue
6. n - ew
grammar.answers:
1. home
2. slow
3. toe
4. June
5. blue
6. new
Five or six right? You can read these.

grammar.title: Writing a word that has o_e, oe, u_e, ue, ew in it
grammar.explanation:
Say the word. Break it into sounds.
One of those sounds needs TWO letters.
Count sounds, then write.
grammar.rule:
home     h - o_e - m        3 sounds, 4 letters
slow     s - l - ow         3 sounds, 4 letters
grammar.workedExample:
You want to write toe.
1. Say it out loud.
2. Break it: t - oe.
3. Which sound needs two letters?
4. Write that pair together.
5. Read it back to check.
grammar.mistake:
One letter for each sound is wrong now.
The new sound takes two letters.
grammar.tip: Count sounds. Some need two letters.
grammar.practice:
Write the word you hear.
1. toe
2. June
3. blue
4. new
5. note
6. few
grammar.answers:
1. toe
2. June
3. blue
4. new
5. note
6. few
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.title: ow says two sounds: cow and slow
grammar.explanation:
You met ow in Unit 14. Cow. Now.
It has a second sound.
In slow it is the long o.
grammar.rule:
The cow sound    cow, now, how, down
The long o       slow, snow, low, grow

Same two letters. Two sounds.
grammar.workedExample:
You see a word with ow in it.
1. Try the cow sound first.
2. Does that make a word you know?
3. If yes, that is it.
4. If no, try the long o.
5. One of the two will be a word.
grammar.mistake:
Deciding before you read wastes time.
Read it one way. Not a word? Read it the other way.
grammar.practice:
Which sound? Say each one out loud.
1. cow
2. slow
3. down
4. snow
5. how
6. grow
grammar.answers:
1. cow
2. slow
3. cow
4. slow
5. cow
6. slow
Five or six right? Your ears are doing the work.

grammar.title: ew is not ow. Look at the letters
grammar.explanation:
These two look alike and are not.
One letter apart, and no sound in common.
This is a looking mistake, not a hearing one.
grammar.rule:
ew    new, few, grew, blew     long u
ow    now, cow, how, down      the cow sound

new  is not  now
few  is not  fow
grammar.workedExample:
You see the word grew.
1. Look at the last two letters.
2. Is it e-w or o-w?
3. It is e-w.
4. So it is long u.
5. g - r - ew. Grew.
grammar.mistake:
Reading ew as ow is the commonest slip here.
Slow down and look at the vowel.
grammar.tip: e-w is long u. o-w is not.
grammar.practice:
Read each word. Write ew or ow.
1. new
2. now
3. few
4. how
5. grew
6. down
grammar.answers:
1. ew
2. ow
3. ew
4. ow
5. ew
6. ow
All six right? You are looking, not guessing.

readings.title: The Trip Home
readings.genre: A short text using known spellings
readings.setting: A long bus journey home in June
readings.passage:
In June I went home.
It was a slow trip.
The bus was blue and new.
I broke my toe on a stone.
Few of us said a thing.
I got home late at night.

readings.title: Two Sounds For ow
readings.setting: The wall card, sixteenth one along
readings.passage:
ow is two sounds.

cow, now, how, down

And ew is neither. New is not now.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — The new sounds
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat each sound.
o_e
oe
u_e
ue
ew
ONE sound each. Not two.
Now say each one three times.
Tap the mic. Say them all.
Check: one sound, or did two slip out?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say one of the new sounds. Say it back.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Read the words
speaking.instructions:
Say each word two ways. Slow, then fast.
1. h - o_e - m ... home
2. s - l - ow ... slow
3. t - oe ... toe
4. J - u_e - n ... June
5. b - l - ue ... blue
6. n - ew ... new
Tap the mic. Say all six both ways.
Check: was the new spelling one sound?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say three sounds. Join them and say the word.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Say it, then write it
speaking.instructions:
For each word: say it, break it, write it.
1. toe
2. June
3. blue
4. new
5. note
6. few
Tap the mic. Say each word and its sounds.
Check: did you say the sounds before you wrote?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for a word with the new spelling. Break it out loud.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Read the list
speaking.instructions:
Read these out loud, straight down the list.
home
slow
toe
June
blue
new
note
few
Do it twice. The second time, try not to stop.
Tap the mic. Read the list twice.
Check: was the second time easier?
speaking.tutor: Read the list to the tutor. Ask which words were not clear.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Two sounds of ow
speaking.instructions:
Say each word. Then say cow or slow.
cow. slow. down. snow. how. grow.
Say the word, then say which sound it has.
Tap the mic. Do all six.
Check: did you get three of each?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say now and snow. Not the same.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — new and now
speaking.instructions:
Say each pair, one after the other.
new, now
few, how
grew, down
They look close. They sound nothing alike.
Tap the mic. Say all three pairs.
Check: did you look at the vowel each time?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say new and now. Say which is which.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Words with the new spelling
writing.prompt:
Say each word. Break it into sounds.
Write two letters for the new sound.
writing.criteria:
Six words.
The new spelling written as a pair.
You read each one back after writing it.
writing.extension: Now write one more word with the same spelling.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Sounds and letters
writing.prompt:
Write each word. Then write two numbers.
How many sounds. How many letters.
writing.criteria:
Six words.
Two numbers beside each one.
The numbers are not the same. That is the point.
writing.extension: Find a word where they ARE the same.

quizzes.q: When you see o_e you should ___.
quizzes.why: Read the pair as one, not as two letters.

quizzes.q: Join the sounds: h - o_e - m. The word is ___.
quizzes.why: The sounds in order make the word.

quizzes.q: Join the sounds: s - l - ow. The word is ___.
quizzes.why: Find the pair first, then read the rest.

quizzes.q: To write a word with the new spelling you ___.
options: write two letters for that sound
write one letter for each sound
quizzes.a: write two letters for that sound
quizzes.why: The new sound is one sound and two letters.

quizzes.q: How many sounds are in home?
quizzes.why: Count what you HEAR. There are more letters than sounds.

options: read the pair as one sound
quizzes.a: read the pair as one sound
quizzes.why: Letter by letter is the slow way here.

quizzes.q: You cannot read a word. What do you do first?
quizzes.why: Find the pair, then read around it.

quizzes.q: Cow and slow both have ow. The sound is ___.
quizzes.why: One is the cow sound. One is long o.

quizzes.q: You see a word with ow in it. You should ___.
options: try one sound, then the other
quizzes.a: try one sound, then the other
quizzes.why: One of the two will be a word you know.

quizzes.q: The word new has ___ at the end.
quizzes.why: Look at the vowel. It is an e, not an o.
One letter apart, and no sound in common.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

This is the whole unit, and it goes against everything Units 2 to 7 taught. Expect a learner to read the letters separately for a while. Do not explain it again; point at the pair and say the one sound, and have them say it back. It is a habit, and habits are built by repetition, not by argument.

teacherNotes.type: Find the pair before reading, not during
teacherNotes.note: Left-to-right letter-by-letter reading breaks on these words, because the learner commits to the first letter's sound before they have seen the second. The move is to scan the word for the pair first. A finger under the pair is enough. It looks like a crutch and it is the skill.

From here to the end of the level there are always more letters than sounds. A learner who counts letters will write a spare letter into every word. Have them say the word and count on their fingers before they write.

teacherNotes.type: ow is the second ambiguous spelling, and that is good news
teacherNotes.note: The learner met this shape in Unit 13 with oo — boot and foot — and the strategy is identical: try one, ask whether it made a word, try the other. Point back to oo explicitly. A second instance of a known pattern is far easier than a new problem, and saying so is most of the work.

teacherNotes.type: ew against ow is an eye error, not an ear one
teacherNotes.note: The two sounds are nothing alike, so a learner who reads new as now has misread the letters rather than mis-heard the sound. Correcting the pronunciation will not help. Point at the vowel and have them say which letter it is.

teacherNotes.type: Eight spellings across two sounds is the peak
teacherNotes.note: This is the densest unit in the level. It does not need to be mastered here — oa, o_e, ow, oe and oo, u_e, ue, ew all come back in reading for years. What must land is that all four in each group say ONE sound, so none of them is a word the learner cannot attempt.

assignment.title: Read and write the new words
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say the sound for each new spelling.
Then read these words, slowly and then faster:
home, slow, toe, June, blue, new
2. Write six of the words from their sounds.
Beside each one, write how many sounds it has.
Listen back before you finish.
